title: How Syracuse's Semiconductor Gamble May Help Save the Rust Belt
title_cn: How Syracuse's Semiconductor Gamble May Help Save the Rust Belt
summary: What does it actually take to bring a Rust Belt city back to life? Micron is building one of the largest semiconductor factories in US history in Syracuse, a city that experienced major job loss after companies including GE, Carrier and General Motors left the area. Rob Simpson of CenterState CEO explains what attracted Micron to the city, local business owner Darin Price talks about what the investment means on the ground, and Brookings economist Joseph Parilla makes the case that Syracuse could be a model for reindustrialization across America. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Birding Apps Bring More People Into the Wild
title_cn: Birding Apps Bring More People Into the Wild
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, writer and photographer Alexandra Marvar explains how apps such as Merlin are making birding easier and more accessible, helping draw new people to a hobby that offers an escape into nature. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Marvar also explores whether technology can remove some of the challenge, learning and satisfaction that traditionally come with identifying birds.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mexico Stresses Sovereignty in US Cooperation
title_cn: Mexico Stresses Sovereignty in US Cooperation

Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, he says Mexico remains cautiously optimistic about ongoing trade negotiations as it seeks relief from US tariffs on automobiles and steel. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Russia Ukraine War Becomes Economic Battle
title_cn: Russia Ukraine War Becomes Economic Battle
summary: New York Times Kyiv bureau chief Andrew Kramer tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia and Ukraine are increasingly targeting each other’s economies as the war shifts toward attacks on energy, transportation and export infrastructure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kramer says Ukraine is using its expanding drone arsenal to target Russia’s oil industry and its ability to finance a prolonged war. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Higher Bond Yields Mark a Return to Normal
title_cn: Higher Bond Yields Mark a Return to Normal

Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz says higher yields have made fixed income more attractive while investors should consider whether strong equity gains have pushed their portfolios away from their intended allocations. (Source: Bloomberg)

title_cn: Northeast Faces Wind, Rain and Coastal Flooding

(Source: Bloomberg)

title: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive
title_cn: Iran War Endgame Remains Elusive

Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Esfandiary says Gulf Arab states are pressing to avoid further escalation as they seek to limit the economic and security damage from the conflict.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The China Trade Problem That Tariffs Alone Can't Fix
title_cn: The China Trade Problem That Tariffs Alone Can't Fix
summary: China ran a $1.2 trillion trade surplus last year, many of its companies don't need to make a profit, and its exports are growing at two to three times the rate of the global economy. Michael Froman, former US Trade Representative under President Obama and now president of the Council on Foreign Relations, tells us why Xi Jinping sees a consumer-led economy as a political threat, and what happens when China finally runs out of countries willing to buy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title_cn: Trump Xi Summit Leaves Big Issues Unresolved

summary: This week, Council on Foreign Relations President Michael Froman breaks down China's export machine, why twenty years of US pressure hasn't worked, and what happens next. Today, Dimensional manages more than $1 trillion. Booth sits down with David Rubenstein to discuss his new book, "Stay Calm," which applies his investment philosophy of staying calm during periods of market volatility, to navigating the uncertainties of life. He's on this week's episode of The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations. This interview was recorded August 10 in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: CORRECT: India’s Quick-Commerce Architect Eyes Long Bets
title_cn: CORRECT: India’s Quick-Commerce Architect Eyes Long Bets
summary:
The man who transformed how urban India eats, dines, and shops, Deepinder Goyal built his food delivery startup Zomato into one of the country’s biggest consumer technology companies, Eternal. At the height of its success, Goyal stepped away from the day-to-day running of the company he built, to turn his attention to a very different set of challenges with a much longer horizon. 

In an exclusive interview on his sprawling residence in Delhi, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with Goyal about the never-ending journeys of founders, his current pursuits, and his quest for a different kind of eternity.

summary: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management Executive Director Katerina Simonetti, BMO Chief FX Strategist Mark McCormick, Jefferies Managing Director & Equity Research Analyst David Katz, Yale University Jackson Institute for Global Affairs Senior Fellow Stephen Roach, Citi Wealth Head of Portfolio Construction & Analytics Olaolu Aganga, Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson, Georgetown Institute of International Economic Law Visiting Scholar Peter Harrell, & Keeneland President & CEO Shannon Arvin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Harrell: US-China Lack of Deliverables Was as Expected
title_cn: Harrell: US-China Lack of Deliverables Was as Expected
summary: Peter Harrell says that the key dynamic is not which country has the upper hand, but that both China and the United States have meaningful leverage: the U.S. through tariffs, export controls, semiconductors, the dollar and AI technology, and China through rare earths, specialty chemicals, and manufacturing scale. Harrell says this mutual leverage helps explain the recent emphasis on “strategic stability” and why both countries may want to ease tensions for now while they work to reduce their dependence on each other. He speaks to Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Patterson: AI Is Crowding Out Demand for US Treasuries
title_cn: Patterson: AI Is Crowding Out Demand for US Treasuries

She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

Simonetti highlights a sharp jump in Treasury volatility, the biggest in a year, alongside a note that stocks are rising as oil retreats on hopes of a U.S.-Iran deal. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Isabelle Lee on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

Accel Partner Matt Weigand, who focuses on late-stage technology investments including AI infrastructure, says the AI boom is the biggest technology cycle Silicon Valley has seen. He also discusses why open-source AI can grow alongside frontier labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI and why trust and safety are becoming key considerations when Accel decides which AI founders to back. He joins Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

And, Microsoft steps back from the race to build a personal chatbot by instead merging the consumer and workplace versions of its Copilot AI assistant into one. (Source: Bloomberg)

He discusses unresolved tensions around trade, Iran, Russia, and Taiwan, as well as the intensifying AI race. He joins Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Trump-Xi Summit Wraps (Podcast)
title_cn: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Trump-Xi Summit Wraps (Podcast)
summary:
President Donald Trump said he would meet again with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in November, following what he said was a successful summit in Washington that was seemingly light on concrete policy outcomes.
